newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Police search for nine missing S.Korean seamen.
newsitem.headline: Police search for nine missing S.Korean seamen.

text.p: South Korean police were searching for nine missing seamen on Monday after a ship carrying a highly flammable chemical capsized off the southwest coast of the Korean peninsula on Sunday.

Marine police in Mokpo said one member of the South Korean crew had been found dead and another, an engineer, was rescued from the 990 deadweight tonne Chuk-yang-ho. It is owned by a shipping company based in the southern port of Pusan.
The missing crew members were believed to be trapped inside the ship and feared dead from gas fumes, police said.
They said the vessel was carrying 800 tonnes of vinyl chloride monomer (VCM), the feedstock for PVC used in production of plastics.
Police originally said the ship was also carrying liquefied petroleum gas but this was later denied.
"Some of the VCM and ship fuel has leaked from the ship," said a police officer. "But we are unsure of how much has been spilled."
The ship, which was carrying 11 tonnes of A-type ship fuel oil, capsized after hitting rocks and was lying partially submerged with only its bow visible.
The coast guard has banned all shipping within a two-mile (3.2 km) radius of the capsized vessel in fear of an explosion.
Police, who are investigating the cause of the accident, said the the ship was on its way from Japan to the South Korean port of Kunsan when it capsized.
